text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.

BARLEY SALE - Tunisia on Thursday bought 100,000 tonnes of optional-origin feed barley at $136.64 per tonne, cost and freight, European grain traders said. The barley is for shipment from May 10 until August 20.

WHEAT AND BARLEY SALE - The Japanese Food Agency said it had bought 100,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat, 45,000 of Canadian wheat, 20,000 of Australian wheat and 20,000 of Australian barley at its weekly tender on Thursday, all for March shipment.
CORN SALES - Korea's Feedgrain Purchase Committee bought 50,000 tonnes of corn from Tradigrain through a private negotiation. Arrival was set by April 30 to Inchon.
- The Philippines bought 100,000 tonnes of corn from China at US$157 per tonne C&F, an Agriculture Department official said. Delivery is set between February 20 and March 25.

- South Korea's National Livestock Cooperatives Federation bought 157,500 tonnes of corn and passed on a tender for 52,500 tonnes due to high prices, an NLCF official said. Shipments were slated for May and August.

CORN SALE - Taiwan's CK group bought a 54,000-tonne shipment of U.S. No.2 corn from Agrex at a tender on Thursday. The CK Group comprises Chia Hsin Flour Feed and Vegetable Oil Corp and some buyers from Taiwan's port city of Kaohsiung. Shipment was slated for March and April.

CORN AND SOYBEAN TENDER - Taiwan's Hui Shung Group on Thursday passed on a tender for a combined shipment comprising 38,500 tonnes of U.S. No.2 soybeans and 16,000 tonnes of U.S. No.2 corn due to high prices, traders said.

WHEAT TENDERS - India's state-run State Trading Corporation said it would decide in the next two days on offers received for its tender to import 50,000 tonnes of wheat. STC last week tendered for the wheat imports, due for shipment by the end of February and for arrival no later than March 31. The tenders closed on Wednesday.
- The CCC said it was seeking up to 40,000 tonnes of U.S. No. 2 soft white wheat, 13.5 pct moisture, for Pakistan. Shipment period was slated for February 20 to March 15.

WHEAT TENDERS - The CCC will tender February 5 for 2,170 tonnes of No.2 hard red winter wheat, ordinary protein, for donation to Uganda. The donation will be made under the World Food Program and will be shipped March 1-25.

- Egypt's main wheat buyer said Tuesday it was back in the market, seeking bids for 50,000 tonnes of Argentine, U.S. or French wheat for loading in March or April. The deadline for bids is 8 a.m. local (0600 GMT) on February 1.
- Results are awaited on Bangladesh's tender for 100,000 tonnes U.S. No.2 wheat or Australian or Canadian winter red/spring wheat for shipment by February 21, traders said.

WHEAT TENDER - Sri Lanka has opened a tender for 100,000 tonnes of optional origin wheat, for delivery in two lots of hard and soft wheat, an official for the Cooperative Wholesale Establishment said. The tender, for 50,000 tonnes each of hard and soft wheat, will close on February 7.

CORN TENDERS - The CCC said it seeks to buy 27,170 tonnes of No. 2 yellow corn for donation to Uganda, Mozambique and Angola. Offers are due on February 5. The CCC said 10,000 tonnes will be donated to Uganda, 9,260 to Mozambique and 7,910 to Angola. Shipment of all three lots was to be March 1-25.
- Turkey will tender February 3 to export 150,000 tonnes of feed barley and 50,000 tonnes of malting barley for shipment in February and March, traders said.
SORGHUM TENDERS - The CCC said it would seek 15,000 tonnes of U.S. no 2 or better sorghum, of which 5,000 tonnes would be for donation to Uganda and 10,000 tonnes for Ethiopia.
The CCC said the shipment period for both tenders was March 1-25. Offers for both were due on February 5.
RICE TENDERS - Syria's General Foreign Trade Organization for Chemicals and Foodstuffs is seeking to buy 12,000 tonnes of white rice for March shipment. Results would be February 3.
- Iraq will tender on February 3 for 30,000 tonnes of U.S. long grain rice under Iraq's "food-for-oil" program. The tender is for two 15,000 tonne positions for April and May delivery.

MARKET TALK - Russia will take delivery of around 25,000 tonnes of Argentine milling wheat in the next few weeks. A senior grains trade source said Tradigrain bought the cargo for delivery to Russia's Far Eastern port of Vladivostok, adding the delivery marks the first time Argentinian wheat appeared on the Russian market in recent years.

... Malaysia has purchased up to 100,000 tonnes of corn for February and March deliveries with the bulk of the imports from China and is in the market to buy more if prices are attractive, trade sources said.
... The Philippines is to buy 205,000 tonnes of 25 percent grade Thai rice, Foreign Minister Prachuab Chaiyasarn said Thursday after returning from a trip to Manila.
